Jacob made a massive tactical mistake, but not in a way many think.

The logic behind taking the early lead and setting the pace because his ending is not the strongest was solid. The mistake was that he kept it so steady.

comment:
I just wanna clear up, that the *only* dressage test that’s actually choreographed to music is the freestyle which you have to qualify for - the first test (qualification round) you do is the same for everyone. The free style test is where riders have required movements and they can come up with the format + music, unlike the first test which you follow the chosen movements ie. do a canter half pass from G to M, then do a flying change past M etc etc… 

And unlike figure skating/ dance the music is always added after the choreography is set! Because it’s just to enhance the visuals it’s not actually supposed to be a dance. And also the music is chosen very specifically! We look at the beat of the gait, for example the trot is 2 beats & each horse has a unique BPM so if it’s like 100BPM we search up 100BPM songs and it’ll be almost impossible to be off time with the music!

@@TokyoQuaSaRどうもそのテディさん含めて現代柔道を嫌ってる日本人の者です。
事情を知らない貴方の為に教えます。
まず日本人は、テディさん個人には強い嫌悪感は余り有りません。しかし現代柔道や今回の2024大会に対して嫌悪感を示している人が多いいです。
理由柔道の本質を理解していない点主に礼をする前のガッツポーズや抱き合う姿など次に団体最後の代表戦でのデジタルルーレットです。日本人はこの件をイカサマだと考えています。特にデジタルである点でありデータをいじるだけで好きに結果を変えれてしまう点などで日本人は怒っています。また不可思議な審判による判定行為は余計に日本人を怒らせました。

最後に私の意見ですが。
審判が待てをしていたのに締め技を外さないなどの危険行為が行われた点や反則技が一本になってしまう判定などは、決して許しては行けないと考えます。
また日本の柔道はスポーツでは、有りません。本来の姿は相手を殺す技でありそれの練習という意味合いです。ですので礼で初めて礼で終わるようになっています。
日本には剣道と言う物がありそれには残心という相手を斬っても油断しない背中を見せないと言う物があります。何故なら相手を斬り損ねた場合には自分が斬られてしまうからです。
命と命のやり取りをしている場でガッツポーズを行う人間は、例えばチャンピオンでも認められるべき存在では無いと私は考えます。

comment:
Ce point de vue de pro est précieux, merci !
Cela dit, ne serait-ce pas le lieu de rappeler que la PSEUDO-force centrifuge n'est que la sensation subjective ressentie par le sujet qui subit deux forces réelles : l'inertie et la centripète ?
author: @michelkuhne5787

comment:
C'est bien de rappeler que la force centrifuge n'est pas une force "réelle" (mais une construction mathématique pour étudier les mouvements circulaires).
Ceci dit l'inertie n'est pas une force non plus.
La force centripète ici correspond à la composante transversale au mouvement de la force de résistance du sol (qui a aussi une composante verticale). 
Les forces réelles appliquées aux coureurs sont donc la gravité, la résistance du sol et les frottements avec l'air.
La résistance du sol va dépendre de la gravité, de l'orientation du coureur (d'où leur inclinaison) et de la force exercée par leurs muscles. La force des muscles est difficile à étudier parce qu'il faut considérer le corps comme différents morceaux, le plus simple pour étudier l'inclinaison est de supposer que le coureur a une vitesse constante et qu'il peut être comparé à une roue (càd un objet rigide avec presque pas de frottements au sol)
author: @ccrouzet

comment:
@@ccrouzet Juste, merci de cette pertinente correction ! 
J'aurais pu faire aussi court en disant "... est soumis à deux contraintes réelles : l'inertie et la force centripète."
Cela dit, la force centrifuge est plus qu'un "truc de matheux" ; elle est certes purement subjective, mais bien réelle pour le sujet, précisément.
Si je me souviens bien, coriolis est aussi une pseudo-force et l'usure asymétrique des rails Nord-Sud est pourtant bien réelle, non ?
author: @michelkuhne5787

comment:
@@michelkuhne5787  oui en fait tout ce dont on parle (centrifuge, centripète, cariolis) correspond bien à des choses réelles d'une manière ou d'une autre (sinon on n'en parlerait pas 😆), mathématique ne veut pas dire fictif.
J'avais pensé que "force élémentaire" serait plus adapté pour faire la distinction entre forces "elementaires" et pseudo-forces, sauf que ce terme correspond déjà à autre chose en physique ! (les 4 interactions élémentaires)

Although I didn't like some moments that were too "woke" and didn't represent France, the opening ceremony wasn't just about that : The fact that the show took place outside for the first time and was a moving show on the Seine was, in my opinion, something special. 
Moreover, we must not forget that  Aya Nakamura performed with the Republican guard, Lady Gaga performed, Celion Dion performed, Gojira performed, there was a cabaret, other athletes (like people doing double dutch etc...) and other dancers (like ballet dancers) performed on the Quais de Seine, there was assassin's creed, the Minions, a horse rider on the Seine, a  beautiful "Marseillaise" anthem sung  etc...
All this to say that yes, the ceremony is very open to criticism due to the overly "woke" choices of the artistic direction, however the show wasn't just about.

If more men are investing their time in watching the olympics and playing those sports, the men participating in those Olympics are going to have a harder time qualifying, meaning the quality will be better. Men’s sport is not just higher quality because men are naturally better, but because there is more competition, and so there are higher stakes and therefore more skill is required. When you become the best Olympian as a woman, you are the best woman. When you become the best Olympian as a man, you are the best human. Men invest their time and money in the Olympics and sport in general a lot more than women do, so yes what gender is watching IS important. We do not need 50% of athletes being women if it takes away from the quality of their performance. If women were more interested in sport I would be all for it, but it shouldn’t be pushed for the sake of just doing it.

comment: I’d like to point out that the design of the U.S. Olympic team's blazer can be traced back to the original boating blazers worn by the Lady Margaret Boat Club of St. John's College, Cambridge, in 1825. Those OG athletic blazers featured distinctive colors and club insignia, setting a precedent for modern iterations. While the inclusion of product placement is a more recent development, the style itself has a rich history that predates contemporary adaptations seen in popular culture, such as the "Never Been Kissed" episode of Glee (November 9, 2010). The evolution of fashion often reflects a delicate balance between tradition and innovation, making the study of fashion history a fascinating journey (and that makes me miss my years in Manhattan even more).
